limitations: Prompt-level isolation only: the worker shared a filesystem with the corpus and key and was instructed not to read them; no sandbox boundary was provisioned.
Token, tool-call and duration figures are the harness totals for the subagent, including reading the task.
The worker acted as its own controller when recording observations.

findings.explanation: escapeDomain calls String.replace with a string pattern, so only the first dot is escaped. For domains ['shop.example','eu.pay.example'] the second dot in eu.pay.example stays a regex wildcard, and origin 'https://eu.pay-example' (a different host) is allowed. Expected false, observed true.

toPence uses Math.trunc(amount * 100). Floating-point multiplication gives 19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999999999998, which truncates to 1998. Input 19.99 should yield 1999 pence; observed 1998. splitAmount inherits the error (splitAmount(19.99, 1) returns [1998]).

hasMore uses end < items.length - 1 where it should use end < items.length. For ['a','b','c'] with pageSize 2, page 1 reports hasMore false although 'c' follows, and collectAll(['a','b','c'], 2) returns ['a','b'], dropping the last element. Expected all three elements; observed two.

When user.role is a single string, rolesOf returns that string and String.prototype.includes performs a substring match. hasRole({ role: 'bowner' }, 'owner') returns true, and canManageBilling({ role: 'no-billing-admin' }) returns true, although neither user holds the named role. The contract requires exact equality.

SORT_PATTERN carries the m flag, so ^ and $ match at line breaks. sort 'name\n1; DELETE FROM orders' passes the test, and the whole string, including the injected newline and text, is placed after ORDER BY through the field + ' ASC' concatenation. The function returns text instead of throwing.

deposit adds amount to account.balance with no check that the sum stays a safe integer. For a balance of Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1 and amount 5, deposit returns normally and leaves an unsafe balance. The contract requires a throw and an unchanged account in that case.

The check rejects only values starting with '//'. The input '/\evil.example/path' passes, and the WHATWG parser treats the backslash as a slash, so resolving against https://app.example gives origin https://evil.example. Expected https://app.example; observed https://evil.example.
